title: Challenge, Not Sign-Off
briefing: Warehouse Operations has submitted its annual risk and control self-assessment (RCSA). Every control is rated 'effective' and every risk 'low'. Benedikt Osei, the Warehouse Director, wants risk to sign it off by Friday.
Your job as the second line is to challenge, not to rubber-stamp.

context.text: The new near-miss reporting is producing data again: 31 reports from warehouses last quarter.
The yard injury at Northgate happened in a warehouse area this RCSA rates as 'low risk'.

evidence.title: Warehouse RCSA summary
evidence.body: 14 risks, all rated low. 22 controls, all 'effective'. No control testing evidence attached. Completed in one 40-minute workshop.

evidence.title: Open internal audit points (warehouses)
evidence.body: Three open points: stock counts not reconciled at two sites (raised 9 months ago); forklift licence checks missing for agency staff; fire door alarms disabled in a chilled store.

evidence.title: Warehouse loss events, last 12 months
evidence.body: Stock write-offs 214,000 (up 40%). Two forklift incidents. One fire service visit (false alarm, door alarms disabled).

questions.prompt: Which points contradict the RCSA's 'all effective' ratings?

options.label: Unreconciled stock counts at two sites with write-offs up 40%
No licence checks for agency forklift drivers, and two forklift incidents
Disabled fire door alarms in a chilled store
The workshop took only 40 minutes
options.feedback: A short workshop is a warning sign about process, but not evidence that a specific rating is wrong.

options.label: The director wants it signed off by Friday
options.feedback: Time pressure is context, not evidence about the controls.

options.label: Meet him with the three contradicting facts, ask what evidence supports each 'effective' rating, and agree which ratings change
options.feedback: Challenge anchored in facts, framed as questions, ending in agreement.

options.label: Sign it off and note your concerns in an email
options.feedback: Second-line sign-off without challenge gives false assurance.

options.label: Reject the whole RCSA and ask them to redo it
options.feedback: Possibly needed, but a blanket rejection without specifics invites a fight and the same answers.

options.label: Escalate straight to the COO
options.feedback: Escalate if he refuses; going over his head first damages the working relationship.

questions.prompt: Benedikt agrees to re-rate one risk now and test the rest. Which one first?

options.label: Fire safety in the chilled store: disabled alarms create a life-safety exposure today
options.feedback: Life safety first, and it is cheap to fix.

options.label: Stock loss: it is the biggest money figure
options.feedback: Important, but money can wait a week; life safety cannot.

options.label: Agency forklift licences
options.feedback: Serious and urgent, but the disabled fire alarms are the more immediate danger.

questions.prompt: Your note to the Risk Committee on the warehouse RCSA says:

options.label: "The self-assessment does not reflect three known control failures. Ratings for fire, stock and forklift safety have been changed with the Warehouse Director; testing of the other 19 controls is due by month end."
options.feedback: States the problem, what has been agreed, and what happens next.

options.label: "Warehouse Operations submitted an unreliable assessment."
options.feedback: True, but it blames without informing and damages the partnership.

options.label: Report only the final agreed ratings
options.feedback: Hides the fact that the first-line process failed, which the committee needs to know.

questions.prompt: To stop this recurring, what evidence will you require with future RCSAs?

options.label: For each key control: a test result (sample, exceptions) and the loss events and audit points mapped to it
options.feedback: Ratings tied to data cannot drift far from reality.

options.label: A two-hour workshop instead of 40 minutes
options.feedback: More time without evidence gives longer opinions.

options.label: A signed declaration from the director
options.feedback: A signature adds accountability but not evidence.

lesson: The second line challenges with evidence and agrees changes with the first line. A self-assessment that contradicts known losses and audit points is not assurance.
